**US stocks in play — 2026-10-30 (midday digest)**

- **Run time:** 12:15 ET fire. **Live intraday quotes pulled at 12:36–12:41 ET** (market open, ~3h20m to the 16:00 ET close).
- **These are live intraday prices, not settled closes** — every number moves until the bell.
- **Session state:** US cash session open. Friday 2026-10-30. Not a US exchange holiday (next closure 11-26, Thanksgiving).
- **Slot:** midday. Liquidity floors applied at the midday scale (price >= $1; market cap >= $50M soft; session $ volume >= ~$2M; RVol a **soft preference**, not a hard gate).
- **Sort note:** Tier A -> Soft-A -> TECH_WATCH -> B -> C.
- **Within each tier, ranked by session USD dollar volume descending.** Tier A and Soft-A carry a material same-session catalyst; TECH_WATCH carries none.
- **Universe scanned:** 11,421 US-listed names (5,615 stocks + 5,806 ETFs) from a full live screener, filtered to 303 that clear price/market-cap/dollar-volume floors with a |move| >= 4%.
- **90 names** were pulled to full intraday chart detail and tiered (22 A / 39 Soft-A / 10 TECH_WATCH / 15 B / 4 C);
- 89 carry live chart data and appear in the CSV.
- **RVol basis:** session volume divided by the **trailing 10 settled sessions** from the same Nasdaq historical series.
- Nasdaq's own `AverageVolume` field was used only as a fallback where the historical endpoint returned fewer than 10 bars; 227 of 227 symbols with RVol have a trailing-10 denominator.
- **Data path (degraded, see Source health):** the skill's primary TradingView / Yahoo Finance MCPs are **not registered in this sandbox** — `tool_search` returns no matches for either.
- The run fell back to HTTP sources (Nasdaq public APIs, stockanalysis.com public quote API, CBOE delayed-quote CDN, CoinGecko) plus `web_search` for catalysts.
- **Every price in this file was cross-checked against two independent providers** (stockanalysis.com quote API + Nasdaq intraday chart endpoint), and the two agreed within tolerance on every tiered name.

---

**The headline**

- This was **one story, not a hundred**: the AI-capex complex broke.
- Intel's Q4 guide came in below the Street on a **PC demand collapse driven by memory prices**, and because Intel is a demand *caller* rather than a supplier, every company downstream of enterprise and consumer hardware got repriced with it —
- semis first, then the AI-infrastructure renters, then the software that sells into them. The transmission order is visible in the tape:
- SOXX -8.4%, SMH -6.9%, then DELL/CRWV/NET/DDOG/ALAB/ARM/CRDO all in the -10% to -12% range on volume that was **light relative to their own 10-day norms** (RVol 0.4–1.2x on most).
- Amazon gapped -5.8% and got bought back to -2.0% on 1.42x RVol — the only mega-cap that fought the tape.

- The caveat that most changes how this reads:
- **almost none of the damage is a fresh company-specific shock.** MU, NVDA, SNDK, WDC, STX, LRCX, AMAT, ANET, TSEM, AXTI, AAOI and COHR all moved without their own news —
- they were dragged by INTC's PC commentary and by the memory-pricing debate it opened.
- On a tape like that, the individual names with genuine same-session catalysts (INTC, RDDT, REGN, CDNA, OSPN, GDYN, BFAM, ATEC) are the tradeable ones and the read-across names are momentum, not information.

- Two more things worth flagging. First, **the selloff is narrow, not systemic**: SPY -1.50% against QQQ -3.13%, with staples +1.70%, energy +1.32%, utilities +0.97% and healthcare +0.96% all green —
- a violent **rotation**, not a liquidation. Second, a **second, unrelated shock ran underneath the tech tape**:
- the record **$6.3B Binance hack** (North Korea's TraderTraitor unit, per TRM Labs) crushed the crypto complex — BTC -4.9%, COIN -12.5%, MSTR -6.3%, HOOD -8.1%, CRCL -8.4% —
- and simultaneously forced **gold and silver into liquidation** (GLD -3.1%, SLV -6.0%, GDX -5.1%) as hot September PCE and a fourth straight monthly gain in crude oil pushed December Fed-hike odds to ~70%.
- Those are two different trades that happened to share a tape.

**Overnight carry — after-close and forward-dated catalysts**

- **Name**: SNDK · **Event**: FQ1 FY2027 results · **When**: after tonight's close (consensus rev $10.72B, adj EPS $46.67)
- **Why it matters**: Already reported after Thursday's close: revenue $11.03B, +378% y/y, beat; adj EPS $49.51 vs $47.15; Q2 guided $12.2-12.6B vs $12.31B est; data-centre revenue +61% q/q to $4.80B; 8-for-1 forward stock split announced; large buyback. And the stock fell 12.3% today anyway — consumer revenue collapsed 29% q/q to $397M as the market "adjusts to higher pricing", and Morningstar cut fair value to $870 from $1,000 on a pricing peak ("pricing growth is decelerating earlier and more quickly than we expected").
- **Name**: 9 reporters · **Event**: MSGK, TXNM, COFS, HOST, ABVC, FBLG, SONM, AMST, PW · **When**: after today's close
- **Why it matters**: The Nasdaq calendar lists these with no time supplied — all are Q3 reporters for today with unconfirmed timing. TXNM Energy ($6.5B cap) and Knickerbocker's ($7.5B) are the material ones.
- **Name**: INTC · **Event**: Kiryat Gat fab restart; 2027 capex step-up · **When**: Q4 2026
- **Why it matters**: The ~$300M Q4 / ~$600M two-quarter revenue hit from the October 14 explosion, plus 2027 capex "up strongly" and no positive free cash flow in 2027. The recovery path is a 2027 story, not a Q4 one.
- **Name**: AGIO · **Event**: Mitapivat sickle-cell sNDA · **When**: PDUFA Feb 1, 2027
- **Why it matters**: Pushed out three months as a "major amendment" after the FDA asked about a REMS; Agios submitted ~9 months of new safety data with no hepatocellular injury of comparable pattern/severity to the thalassemia trials, and says it is launch-ready.
- **Name**: EXEL · **Event**: Zanzalintinib · **When**: PDUFA Mar 3, 2027 · **Why it matters**: Newly assigned; the second leg of the pipeline behind CABOMETYX.
- **Name**: INSM · **Event**: ARIKAYCE sBLA for MAC lung disease · **When**: PDUFA Jan 28, 2027 · **Why it matters**: Carried from the 10-29 digest; priority review granted.
- **Name**: IOVA · **Event**: POSITILITY precision-cohort enrolment · **When**: Nov 2026
- **Why it matters**: Carried forward. The 59.1% biomarker-selected subgroup was the only thing that got the stock bid; enrolment is the next proof point.
- **Name**: PURR · **Event**: HYPE token unlock · **When**: Nov 6 · **Why it matters**: Carried forward. A DAT proxy is only as good as its token.
- **Name**: DASH / CART · **Event**: DoorDash $65.00/share acquisition of Maplebear · **When**: close late 2027 / H1 2028
- **Why it matters**: Carried forward. CART closed 12.1% below terms yesterday — the spread is deal risk, not an arbitrage.
- **Name**: ADT · **Event**: Go-shop window opens · **When**: Nov 3
- **Why it matters**: Carried forward. Rival bids are the only thing that can lift a stock already below its $10 cash terms.
- **Name**: Macro · **Event**: US midterms; monthly jobs report; December FOMC · **When**: Nov 3; early Nov; Dec
- **Why it matters**: Reuters: midterms, a heavy earnings slate and the jobs report "will further test stock investors next week, after a series of setbacks for the market-leading AI trade." The Fed held rates this week but left the door open to a December hike (~70% priced) after September PCE rose 0.5% — the largest monthly increase since March. Crude is on a fourth monthly gain on Strait of Hormuz supply risk, which is itself an inflation input.
- **Name**: Crypto · **Event**: Binance withdrawals resume · **When**: ~45 hours
- **Why it matters**: $3B frozen; recovery still needs court orders. A failure to restart cleanly is the risk case for COIN, MSTR, HOOD and CRCL.

**Method and caveats**

- **These are live intraday prices at 12:36-12:41 ET, not settled closes.** The session is still open with ~3h20m to the bell.
- Every figure moves; this digest is a snapshot, not a closing statement. Unlike the 10-29 close digest, no price here should be treated as final.
- **The TradingView and Yahoo MCPs named in the skill do not exist in this sandbox**, and Yahoo's HTTP APIs are 429-throttled and Finviz is Cloudflare-403.
- The entire data path is HTTP-based. Nasdaq's public APIs and stockanalysis.com were used instead. This is a **degraded but not failed** run:
- the substitute path delivered live quotes, intraday bars, prior closes, session volume, trailing-10 volume history and market cap for every name in the digest.
- **The Nasdaq bulk screener was verified stale and excluded from pricing.** It returned a previous session's prices under an HTTP 200.
- Every price here comes either from the Nasdaq intraday chart endpoint or the stockanalysis quote API, and the two were cross-checked against each other on all 87 tiered names.
- **Nasdaq's chart endpoint includes premarket bars from 04:00 ET.** Open gaps, day ranges and close-position figures were computed from the **09:30-16:00 ET window only**.
- Two independent definitions of "open" disagree slightly (first RTH print vs the official opening print) —
- a handful of names differ by 1-6% on that field alone, which is why INTC's open gap reads -26.10% from the 09:30 bar against the ~-25.7% official open.
- **RVol is the trailing 10 settled sessions from the same Nasdaq historical series.** 227 of 227 names with an RVol have a trailing-10 denominator;
- the Nasdaq `AverageVolume` field was used only where historical returned fewer than 10 bars, and is labelled `nasdaq_avg` in the working data. **A mid-session RVol is structurally understated** —
- the denominator is a full day and the numerator is a partial day — so every RVol here understates the full-session ratio by roughly the fraction of the session elapsed.
- It is still directionally valid for comparing names against their own norms, which is what tiering uses it for.
- **Tier A mixes two different things, deliberately.** INTC, AMZN, RDDT, COIN, ATEC, BFAM, VRRM and SNDK carry genuine same-session catalysts (INTC's guide, AMZN's miss and holiday guide, Reddit's traffic collapse, Coinbase's revenue miss plus the Binance hack, Alphatec's miss and guidance cut, Bright Horizons' impairment and guidance cut, Verra Mobility's CEO change, Sandisk's pricing-peak selloff).
- **The other large-cap names in Tier A — MU, NVDA, AMD, LITE, MRVL, SKHY, DELL, NBIS, BE, CRWV, STX, LRCX, COHR, AAOI, QCOM —
- carry a catalyst that is either a read-across or a sector event, not their own news.** They are ranked by dollar volume because they are what moved, but they are not the same kind of trade as INTC.
- **On a tape this correlated, individual catalysts get overwhelmed by the macro driver.** In the 10-29 digest six of the largest single-name dislocations were guidance events inside a calm index.
- Today the index itself was moving (-1.50% SPY, -3.13% QQQ, VIX +16.7%), so the marginal information in any single print is lower than usual.
- The tape rewards *relative* strength, which is why AMZN (+0.6pp against SPY), REGN, CBOE, MEOH, EXEL, GDYN and ULH stand out.
- **ARI's apparent -63.6% is a dividend artifact, not a move.** ARI's $4.10 quarterly dividend went ex-date today;
- the raw prior close of $6.45 is not comparable to the $2.35 dividend-adjusted reference. On an adjusted basis the stock is flat.
- It is not a mover and is listed in Tier C only to prevent a false read.
- **UCFI was excluded entirely** —
- the only quote available for it carried a 2025-10-01 date, so it is a stale bar rather than a live session, despite appearing in the live screener universe.
- **Halt status is unverified for every name** (see Halt watch).
- **No float data was available in this run**, so the skill's low-float flag could not be applied on evidence.
- Names where float is a genuine risk (AIOK at $100M market cap on $188M turnover, NRXP at $90M cap on 13.26x RVol, NFE at $70M cap, ULH/RMNI on $2-4M turnover) are called out inline instead.
- **The digest is not a close.** A later run of this cron on the same date may publish a different, settled set of prices;
- if it does, that file supersedes this one for closing purposes.
